items.text: Know what your business is worth. Before you go to market.

The Pre-Market Assessment gives you an indicative valuation range, the earnings behind it and a 90-day plan to strengthen both. Three working sessions and one written assessment. You do not need to have decided to sell.
The Pre-Market Assessment · The first read

Three steps, each deeper than the last. The Pre-Market Assessment gives you an indicative valuation range, your adjusted earnings as you report them, the adjustments a buyer is most likely to question, and a 90-day plan. The preparation review traces every figure to source. The Sell-Side QoE is the report. You can stop after any step, and nothing reaches a buyer without your written permission.

The first read: an indicative valuation range, your adjusted earnings as you report them, the adjustments a buyer is most likely to question, and a 90-day plan. For owners who may sell in two years or never.

The full trace: revenue reconciled to bank deposits, every adjustment marked supported or unsupported with the document that decides it, customers, contracts and licenses read the way a buyer will. Non-attest, and yours to keep.
The report, from the independent CPA firm Capital Row partners with, built on the record the first two steps assembled. A buyer’s team meets reconciled schedules instead of a blank page.
Scope and fee are agreed in writing before any work begins.

items.text: The Pre-Market Assessment · Why it matters
Most owners arrive at the sale without a read on their own numbers.
The valuation gap is the most cited reason a deal does not close, and it is a gap between what the owner expects and what the records support. The assessment reads the records first.
Sellers with under a year of exit planning
Across five deal-size segments in the lower middle market, the share of sellers who arrived at the sale with less than a year of planning, or none. IBBA and M&A Source, Market Pulse, Q2 2026.
Engagements that died on the valuation gap
Share of investment bankers’ engagements that did not close because of the gap between the owner’s price and the market’s. Pepperdine, 2024. Two thirds of those gaps were 11 to 30 percent.
Broken letters that ended on the earnings
Share of seventy-five collapsed letters of intent in 2025 where adjusted earnings were not what was presented. Double the share of two years earlier.
In the lower middle market, in the second quarter of 2026. The assessment is the read that comes before the year.

sections.name: Plain answers, then a conversation if you want one.

items.text: Plain answers, then a conversation if you want one.
What do I need to send?

To start, nothing but a conversation. The assessment begins with an agreed information request: the financial statements as you keep them, the customer list by revenue, and the adjustments you would propose. No financial documents through the website.
Three working sessions and one written assessment, usually inside a month, with a 90-day plan at the end of it.
Is the valuation range a number I can quote?
It is an indicative range for your own planning, with the assumptions written down. It is not an appraisal, and it is not a price.
You decide. Sell now, sell later, keep building, or take the deeper step: the preparation review that traces every figure to source.
You. Nothing from your assessment reaches a buyer, or anyone else, without your written permission.
Scope and fee are agreed in writing before any work begins, once we know what the business needs.
